questions.text: The organelle known as the powerhouse of the cell is the
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration is completed in the mitochondrion, which releases most of the cell's energy in the form of ATP.

questions.text: Protein synthesis in a cell takes place on the
questions.explanation: Ribosomes translate messenger RNA into polypeptide chains, so they are the site of protein synthesis.

questions.text: The cell organelles called suicide bags because of their digestive enzymes are the
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that can digest the cell's own contents if the organelle bursts.

questions.text: The cell wall of a plant cell is mainly composed of
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are chiefly cellulose; chitin occurs in fungal walls and peptidoglycan in bacterial walls.

questions.text: The cell was first observed and named by
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke in 1665 examined a thin slice of cork under his microscope and called the compartments he saw cells.

questions.text: The nucleus of the cell was discovered by
questions.explanation: Robert Brown described the nucleus in plant cells in 1831.

questions.text: The main function of the Golgi apparatus is
options: Packaging and secretion of cell products
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, packages and dispatches materials made in the endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.text: The largest organ of the human body is the
questions.explanation: The skin covers the entire body surface and is the largest organ by both weight and area.

questions.text: The largest gland in the human body is the
questions.explanation: The liver is the largest gland; it secretes bile and performs numerous metabolic functions.

questions.text: The number of bones in the normal adult human skeleton is
questions.explanation: An adult skeleton has 206 bones; a newborn has about 270, many of which fuse during growth.

questions.text: The longest bone in the human body is the
questions.explanation: The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest and strongest bone of the human body.

questions.text: The smallest bone in the human body is the
questions.explanation: The stapes, or stirrup bone, of the middle ear is the smallest bone in the body.

questions.text: The structural and functional unit of the kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons, which filter blood and form urine.

questions.text: The structural and functional unit of the nervous system is the
questions.explanation: The neuron, or nerve cell, transmits impulses; the axon is only a part of a neuron.

questions.text: The gland known as the master gland of the human body is the
questions.explanation: The pituitary secretes hormones that control the activity of most other endocrine glands.

questions.text: The largest artery of the human body is the
questions.explanation: The aorta leaves the left ventricle and distributes oxygenated blood to the whole body.

questions.text: Bile secreted by the liver is stored in the
questions.explanation: Bile made in the liver is concentrated and stored in the gall bladder before release into the duodenum.

questions.text: The voice box of the human respiratory tract is the
questions.explanation: The larynx houses the vocal cords, whose vibration produces sound.

questions.text: The number of teeth in a normal adult human being is
questions.explanation: A complete adult set has 32 permanent teeth, compared with 20 milk teeth in a child.

questions.text: The sheet of muscle separating the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity is the
questions.explanation: The diaphragm separates the chest from the abdomen and contracts during inhalation to enlarge the chest cavity.

questions.text: Urea is chiefly formed in the
questions.explanation: The liver converts ammonia from protein breakdown into urea, which the kidneys then excrete.

questions.text: The blood group known as the universal donor is
questions.explanation: Group O red cells carry neither A nor B antigen, so they are not attacked by the recipient's anti-A or anti-B antibodies.

questions.text: The blood group known as the universal recipient is
questions.explanation: Group AB plasma contains neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies, so blood of any ABO group can be received.

questions.text: The ABO system of human blood groups was discovered by
questions.explanation: Karl Landsteiner identified the ABO blood groups in 1901 and received the Nobel Prize for the work.

questions.text: The Rh factor of human blood takes its name from the
questions.explanation: The antigen was first detected in the blood of the rhesus monkey, hence the name Rh factor.

questions.text: In an adult human being, red blood cells are produced mainly in the
questions.explanation: Red bone marrow is the site of erythrocyte formation after birth; the liver performs this role only in the foetus.

questions.text: The average life span of a human red blood cell is about
questions.explanation: Erythrocytes survive roughly 120 days before being destroyed, mainly in the spleen.

questions.text: The metal present in haemoglobin is
questions.explanation: Each haem group of haemoglobin contains an iron atom that binds oxygen reversibly.

questions.text: Clotting of blood is brought about mainly by
questions.explanation: Platelets, or thrombocytes, collect at a wound and set off the reactions that form a fibrin clot.

questions.text: The straw-coloured fluid in which blood cells remain suspended is called
questions.explanation: Plasma is the fluid part of whole blood; serum is plasma from which clotting proteins have been removed.

questions.text: A mature human red blood cell lacks a
questions.explanation: Mature erythrocytes lose their nucleus, which leaves more room for haemoglobin.

questions.text: The natural pacemaker of the human heart is the
questions.explanation: The sinoatrial node in the right atrium generates the impulse that sets the heart rate.

questions.text: The circulation of blood in the human body was first described by
questions.explanation: William Harvey demonstrated in 1628 that blood circulates in a closed circuit driven by the heart.

questions.text: Oxygenated blood is carried from the lungs to the heart by the
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein is the only vein carrying oxygenated blood, returning it from the lungs to the left atrium.

questions.text: The normal blood pressure of a healthy adult is taken as
questions.explanation: A systolic pressure of about 120 mm Hg and a diastolic pressure of about 80 mm Hg is regarded as normal.

questions.text: The valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle is the
questions.explanation: The bicuspid or mitral valve guards the left atrioventricular opening; the tricuspid valve lies on the right side.

questions.text: The pH of normal human blood is approximately
questions.explanation: Blood is slightly alkaline and is buffered at a pH of about 7.35 to 7.45.

questions.text: Deficiency of vitamin C in the diet causes
questions.explanation: Lack of ascorbic acid weakens connective tissue, producing scurvy with bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

questions.text: Deficiency of vitamin D in children causes
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is needed for calcium absorption; without it bones soften and deform, a condition called rickets.

questions.text: Night blindness results from the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is required to make rhodopsin, the pigment of the rod cells that gives vision in dim light.

questions.text: Beriberi is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Beriberi results from a lack of thiamine, vitamin B1, and affects the nerves and heart.

questions.text: Pellagra is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Pellagra follows a shortage of niacin, vitamin B3, and shows as dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia.

questions.text: Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 is needed for the maturation of red blood cells; its lack produces pernicious anaemia.

questions.text: The vitamin essential for the normal clotting of blood is
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is required by the liver to make prothrombin and other clotting factors.

questions.text: The chemical name of vitamin C is
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid; retinol is vitamin A and calciferol is vitamin D.

questions.text: Which of the following vitamins is water soluble?
questions.explanation: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble, while vitamin C and the B group dissolve in water.

questions.text: The metal present in vitamin B12 is
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12, cyanocobalamin, contains a cobalt atom at the centre of its corrin ring.

questions.text: Goitre is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed to make thyroxine; without it the thyroid enlarges, producing goitre.

questions.text: The chemical name of vitamin E is
questions.explanation: Vitamin E is tocopherol, an antioxidant that protects cell membranes.

questions.text: Insulin is secreted by the
questions.explanation: The beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin.

questions.text: Diabetes mellitus is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Insufficient insulin prevents cells from taking up glucose, so blood sugar rises and sugar appears in the urine.

questions.text: The pancreatic hormone that raises the level of glucose in the blood is
questions.explanation: Glucagon from the alpha cells of the pancreas converts stored glycogen into glucose, raising blood sugar.

questions.text: The hormone released in large amounts during fear or anger is
questions.explanation: Adrenaline from the adrenal medulla prepares the body for fight or flight by raising heart rate and blood sugar.

questions.text: Excessive secretion of growth hormone during childhood results in
questions.explanation: Oversecretion of growth hormone before the growing ends of bones close causes abnormal height, called gigantism.

questions.text: Deficiency of thyroxine in infancy leads to
questions.explanation: Lack of thyroxine in infancy stunts physical growth and mental development, a condition called cretinism.

questions.text: The level of calcium in the blood is regulated by
questions.explanation: Parathormone from the parathyroid glands raises blood calcium by mobilising it from bone.

questions.text: The principal male sex hormone is
questions.explanation: Testosterone is secreted by the testes and controls male secondary sexual characters.

questions.text: The digestion of starch begins in the
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase in the mouth starts breaking starch down into maltose.

questions.text: The digestion of protein begins in the
questions.explanation: Pepsin, activated by hydrochloric acid in the stomach, begins the breakdown of proteins into peptides.

questions.text: The acid present in human gastric juice is
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid makes the stomach contents acidic, activates pepsin and kills many swallowed microbes.

questions.text: Most of the absorption of digested food takes place in the
questions.explanation: The villi lining the small intestine give a huge surface for absorbing digested nutrients.

questions.text: The chief function of the large intestine is the absorption of
questions.explanation: The large intestine reabsorbs most of the water from the undigested residue before faeces are formed.

questions.text: Bile assists in the digestion of
questions.explanation: Bile salts emulsify fats into tiny droplets so that lipase can act on them more easily.

questions.text: The vermiform appendix in man is attached to the
questions.explanation: The appendix is a narrow vestigial tube projecting from the caecum at the start of the large intestine.

questions.text: Exchange of gases in the lungs takes place in the
questions.explanation: The thin, moist walls of the alveoli are surrounded by capillaries, allowing oxygen and carbon dioxide to diffuse.

questions.text: The energy currency of the living cell is
questions.explanation: Adenosine triphosphate stores energy in its phosphate bonds and releases it wherever the cell needs it.

questions.text: During strenuous exercise, muscle cells respiring anaerobically produce
questions.explanation: When oxygen supply falls short, glucose is converted to lactic acid, which causes muscle fatigue and cramp.

questions.text: Carbon monoxide is poisonous to human beings because it
options: Combines with haemoglobin more readily than oxygen
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin far more strongly than oxygen does, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and starving tissues of oxygen.

questions.text: The flap of cartilage that prevents food from entering the windpipe during swallowing is the
questions.explanation: The epiglottis folds over the opening of the larynx while food is being swallowed.

questions.text: Malaria in human beings is caused by a
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the protozoan parasite Plasmodium, which multiplies in the liver and red blood cells.

questions.text: Malaria is transmitted to man by the
questions.explanation: Only the female Anopheles takes blood meals and thus transfers Plasmodium from person to person.

questions.text: Dengue fever is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: The Aedes aegypti mosquito, which bites mostly by day, carries the dengue virus.

questions.text: The causative organism of tuberculosis is
questions.explanation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, identified by Robert Koch, causes tuberculosis and spreads through droplets.

questions.text: AIDS is caused by
questions.explanation: The human immunodeficiency virus destroys helper T cells and so cripples immunity.

questions.text: Cholera is caused by
questions.explanation: The bacterium Vibrio cholerae spreads through contaminated water and causes severe watery diarrhoea.

questions.text: Typhoid fever is caused by
questions.explanation: Salmonella typhi, taken in with contaminated food or water, causes typhoid fever.

questions.text: Rabies is usually transmitted to man through the
questions.explanation: The rabies virus is present in the saliva of infected animals and enters through a bite wound.

questions.text: Sleeping sickness is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: The tsetse fly of tropical Africa carries the protozoan Trypanosoma that causes sleeping sickness.

questions.text: Bubonic plague is transmitted to man mainly by the
questions.explanation: The rat flea carries the plague bacterium Yersinia pestis from infected rodents to human beings.

questions.text: Kala azar, or visceral leishmaniasis, is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: The bite of an infected sand fly transfers the protozoan Leishmania to human beings.

questions.text: Hepatitis is a disease affecting the
questions.explanation: Hepatitis means inflammation of the liver and is most often caused by viruses A, B, C, D or E.

questions.text: Antibiotics such as penicillin are effective against bacteria but not against
questions.explanation: Viruses have no cell wall or metabolic machinery of their own, so antibacterial antibiotics do not affect them.

questions.text: Penicillin was discovered by
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming noticed in 1928 that the mould Penicillium notatum killed bacteria on his culture plate.

questions.text: The first vaccine, used against smallpox, was developed by
questions.explanation: Edward Jenner showed in 1796 that inoculation with cowpox material protected against smallpox.

questions.text: The BCG vaccine gives protection against
questions.explanation: Bacillus Calmette Guerin vaccine is given in infancy to protect against tuberculosis.

questions.text: Oral rehydration salts are given chiefly in the treatment of
questions.explanation: ORS replaces the water and salts lost in diarrhoea and so prevents dehydration.

questions.text: Vaccination protects a person by producing
questions.explanation: A vaccine makes the body produce its own antibodies and memory cells, which is active immunity.

questions.text: The number of chromosomes in a normal human body cell is
questions.explanation: Human somatic cells carry 46 chromosomes, that is 23 pairs, of which one pair determines sex.

questions.text: The sex chromosomes of a normal human male are
questions.explanation: Males carry one X and one Y chromosome, while females carry two X chromosomes.

questions.text: The sex of a human child is determined by the
questions.explanation: The ovum always carries an X chromosome, so the sex depends on whether the sperm carries X or Y.

questions.text: The father of genetics is
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel worked out the laws of inheritance and is regarded as the father of genetics.

questions.text: The double helix model of DNA was proposed by
questions.explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick described the double helical structure of DNA in 1953.

questions.text: The nitrogenous base present in RNA but not in DNA is
questions.explanation: RNA carries uracil in place of the thymine found in DNA.

questions.text: Down syndrome results from an extra copy of chromosome number
questions.explanation: Down syndrome, or trisomy 21, occurs when three copies of chromosome 21 are present instead of two.

questions.text: Haemophilia is an inherited disorder in which
options: Red cells are produced in excess
questions.explanation: Haemophilia is a sex-linked disease caused by the absence of a clotting factor, so bleeding continues for a long time.

questions.text: Photosynthesis in a plant cell takes place in the
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps light energy for the manufacture of food.

questions.text: The green pigment of plants that traps light energy is
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly red and blue light and reflects green, giving leaves their colour.

questions.text: The metal present in the chlorophyll molecule is
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll has a magnesium atom at the centre of its porphyrin ring, in contrast to the iron in haemoglobin.

questions.text: The loss of water in the form of vapour from the aerial parts of a plant is called
questions.explanation: Transpiration takes place mainly through the stomata of leaves and helps draw water up the plant.

questions.text: Water and mineral salts are conducted in a plant by the
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels carry water and dissolved minerals upwards from the roots to the leaves.

questions.text: The minute pores in a leaf through which gases are exchanged are called
questions.explanation: Each stoma is bounded by two guard cells that open and close the pore.

questions.text: Bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of leguminous plants belong to the genus
questions.explanation: Rhizobium lives symbiotically in the root nodules of legumes and converts atmospheric nitrogen into usable compounds.

questions.text: The plant hormone chiefly responsible for cell elongation in shoots is
questions.explanation: Auxin promotes elongation of cells behind the shoot tip; the other three are animal hormones.

questions.text: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from
questions.explanation: In the light reaction, water is split into hydrogen and oxygen, and it is this oxygen that escapes.

questions.text: Water enters the root hairs of a plant mainly by the process of
questions.explanation: Soil water passes through the root hair membrane into the more concentrated cell sap by osmosis.

questions.text: The chief source of energy in a normal human diet is
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates supply most of the body's energy, providing about four kilocalories per gram.

questions.text: The nutrients mainly required for the growth and repair of body tissues are
questions.explanation: Proteins supply the amino acids from which new tissue and enzymes are built.

questions.text: Kwashiorkor in children is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor follows a diet badly short of protein and shows swelling of the limbs and abdomen.

questions.text: Which food component supplies the greatest amount of energy per gram?
questions.explanation: Fat yields about nine kilocalories per gram, roughly twice as much as carbohydrate or protein.

questions.text: The roughage of the human diet consists mainly of
questions.explanation: Cellulose from plant foods cannot be digested by man but adds bulk that keeps the bowel moving.
